boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Iowa
boards.description: Ten currently documented food stops in Iowa City with late service windows; confirm availability before leaving.

cards.title: Falbo Bros Pizza
cards.subtitle: 457 S Gilbert St, Iowa City
cards.notes: Use the official ordering page to check the day’s status, then plan a pickup from this Gilbert Street pizza counter.
cards.short_summary: Pizza pickup with posted service through 2 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Falbo Bros Pizza lists its Iowa City address as 457 S Gilbert St and posts hours of 11 AM–2 AM.
cards.source_title: Falbo Bros Pizza — Iowa City
cards.access_notes: Official site posts hours of 11:00 AM–2:00 AM; verify before travel.

cards.title: Gumby's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 702 S Gilbert St, Suite 103, Iowa City
cards.notes: Check the official schedule before heading south of downtown; it lists late-night delivery and an Iowa City storefront.
cards.short_summary: Pizza and wings with late posted delivery hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Gumby's official Iowa City page lists 702 S Gilbert St, Suite 103 and service until 2:45 AM Monday–Saturday, 1:45 AM Sunday.
cards.source_title: Gumby's Pizza — Iowa City, IA
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Mon–Fri 2 PM–2:45 AM; Sat 11 AM–2:45 AM; Sun 11 AM–1:45 AM.

cards.title: Pancheros Downtown
cards.subtitle: 32 S Clinton St, Iowa City
cards.notes: Use the location’s order options for a downtown pickup, and consult its official page for the applicable late closing time.
cards.short_summary: Downtown burrito stop with service as late as 3 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Pancheros lists its downtown Iowa City location at 32 S Clinton St, with closing at 2 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 3 AM Thursday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Pancheros Mexican Grill — Iowa City (Downtown)
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 10:30 AM–2 AM Sun–Wed and 10:30 AM–3 AM Thu–Sat.

cards.entity_name: Papa Johns Pizza — S Gilbert St
cards.title: Papa Johns on S Gilbert
cards.subtitle: 307 S Gilbert St, Iowa City
cards.notes: Choose carryout or delivery from this Gilbert Street location, checking the posted schedule for the day before ordering.
cards.short_summary: Carryout or delivery pizza with 1–2 AM closing windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists 307 S Gilbert St in Iowa City and Friday–Saturday delivery until 2 AM, with carryout until 1:45 AM.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Pizza — 307 S Gilbert St
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Fri–Sat delivery until 2 AM and carryout until 1:45 AM; other days vary.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on South 1st
cards.subtitle: 805 South 1st Avenue #2, Iowa City
cards.notes: Use the location page to choose delivery or carryout, especially when its Friday and Saturday schedule extends later.
cards.short_summary: Chain pizza pickup or delivery with 1 AM weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut lists its Iowa City location at 805 South 1st Avenue #2 and posted restaurant hours until 1 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Pizza Hut — 805 South 1st Avenue
cards.access_notes: Official hours list 9 AM–1 AM Friday and Saturday; midnight closing Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Highway 6
cards.subtitle: 901 Highway 6 E, Iowa City
cards.notes: This drive-through location is an option when you have transportation; use the official locator to confirm the selected service mode.
cards.short_summary: Drive-through food with posted service as late as 4 AM.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists its Iowa City location at 901 Highway 6 E, with drive-through hours until 4 AM Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 901 Highway 6 E
cards.access_notes: Official drive-through hours: until 2 AM Sun–Wed, 3 AM Thu, and 4 AM Fri–Sat.

cards.title: Domino's on South Gilbert
cards.subtitle: 1534 S Gilbert St, Iowa City
cards.notes: Order online or call ahead for delivery or takeout, then confirm the live closing time on the location page.
cards.short_summary: South Iowa City pizza location that posts a 1 AM close.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's official location page identifies the store at 1534 S Gilbert St in Iowa City and states it is open until 1 AM.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza — 1534 S Gilbert St
cards.access_notes: Official location page displayed “Open Today Until 1:00 AM”; live hours can vary by day.

cards.entity_name: Luna's Tacos Family Kitchen Food Truck
cards.title: Luna's Tacos Food Truck
cards.subtitle: Iowa City Ped Mall, across from Aspen Leaf
cards.notes: Find the seasonal Ped Mall truck only during its listed February–December run, and confirm the nightly setup before going.
cards.short_summary: Seasonal Ped Mall food truck with a 2:30 AM posted close.
cards.evidence_claim: Luna's Tacos lists its food truck in the Iowa City Ped Mall, across from Aspen Leaf, operating February–December from 9 PM–2:30 AM.
cards.source_title: Luna's Tacos Family Kitchen
cards.access_notes: Official site lists the food truck February–December, 9 PM–2:30 AM; its restaurant has different hours.

cards.title: Uncle Sun
cards.subtitle: 100 S Linn St, Iowa City
cards.notes: Check the day-specific schedule before making this Linn Street pickup; late service is listed only Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: Chinese-food pickup with 2 AM service on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Uncle Sun lists its Iowa City location at 100 S Linn St and posts 5 PM–2 AM hours Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Uncle Sun — Iowa City Contact
cards.access_notes: Official hours: 5 PM–2 AM Wednesday–Saturday; midnight Monday and Sunday; closed Tuesday.

cards.title: Marco's Grilled Cheese
cards.subtitle: 117 N Linn St, Iowa City
cards.notes: Use the North Linn Street address and plan for the late Thursday–Saturday window posted by the downtown district.
cards.short_summary: Northside grilled-cheese restaurant with 2 AM weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Iowa City Downtown District lists Marco's Grilled Cheese at 117 N Linn St and hours until 2 AM Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Iowa City Downtown District — Marco's Grilled Cheese
cards.access_notes: Downtown District lists 11 AM–2 AM Thursday–Saturday; Monday–Wednesday until 11 PM and Sunday until 9 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Iowa destinations with documented uses for studying, gathering, cultural activity, and recreation.

cards.title: Set up a shared work session
cards.subtitle: Main Library, first floor
cards.notes: Reserve a group room through Office 365 or in person, then use its monitor and writeable glass to keep a project visible to everyone.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaboration hub with reservable rooms and open group areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons has 22 student-reservable group spaces, including private rooms and open areas with writing surfaces and laptop-connectable monitors.
cards.source_title: Group Spaces | University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Student reservations are made online or in person; group rooms have specific reservation rules.

cards.title: Choose a quieter floor for focused reading
cards.subtitle: Main Library, upper floors
cards.notes: Use the quiet areas on the third through fifth floors when you need independent reading time, and take calls to the central corridors.
cards.short_summary: Designated quiet seating separates concentrated work from first-floor group activity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library identifies quiet study seating on the third floor and in east and west book-stack areas on the fourth and fifth floors.
cards.source_title: Main Library study spaces and locker information | University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Quiet-space guidance permits individual work and asks users to keep conversations quiet.

cards.title: Meet outside with an Old Capitol view
cards.subtitle: South of the Iowa Memorial Union
cards.notes: Plan an outdoor game, information table, or student-organization event here; route organized reservations through IMU Event Services.
cards.short_summary: A campus green used for outdoor activities, fairs, concerts, and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: UI identifies Hubbard Park as the green space south of the IMU and lists outdoor games, social events, student-org fairs, concerts, and information tables as uses.
cards.source_title: Hubbard Park | Iowa Memorial Union
cards.access_notes: Organized events require coordination with the IMU Event Services Office.

cards.title: Use the fireplace lounge between classes
cards.subtitle: Iowa Memorial Union
cards.notes: Bring reading or a laptop to the fireplace lounge, then use the surrounding IMU tables and Wi-Fi for a low-key study break.
cards.short_summary: A named IMU lounge among the union's shared public spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The IMU describes studying by the fireplace in Hubbard Commons and identifies the Hubbard Commons fireplace lounge as a shared public space.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Iowa Memorial Union
cards.access_notes: The IMU lists Wi-Fi, study tables, computer labs, and group-study meeting rooms; some technology access requires a HawkID.

cards.title: Check the public performance calendar
cards.subtitle: 93 E. Burlington Street
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled public performance or presentation, then arrive with time to orient yourself in the downtown music building.
cards.short_summary: The School of Music's downtown building pairs performance spaces with the Rita Benton Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Music says Voxman hosts more than 350 yearly public performances and presentations and includes acoustically designed performance and practice spaces.
cards.source_title: Facilities | University of Iowa School of Music
cards.access_notes: The School of Music posts building hours and notes that holiday and academic-break hours differ.

cards.title: See the Writers’ Workshop’s historic home
cards.subtitle: 507 N. Clinton Street
cards.notes: Walk by the historic house and connect its preserved front section with the Iowa Writers’ Workshop that has been based here since 1997.
cards.short_summary: A historic Iowa City house adapted as the home of the Iowa Writers’ Workshop.
cards.evidence_claim: University Facilities identifies Dey House as the Iowa Writers’ Workshop’s home and says the Workshop has occupied it since 1997.
cards.source_title: Dey House | University of Iowa Facilities Management
cards.access_notes: This is an academic building; observe posted access guidance and do not assume interior public access.

cards.title: Explore the landmark at the Pentacrest
cards.subtitle: 21 N. Clinton Street
cards.notes: Use the museum’s visit and calendar information to plan a daytime stop, then connect the building’s Iowa history with the surrounding Pentacrest.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark and University of Iowa museum in the Old Capitol.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old Capitol Museum describes Old Capitol as a National Historic Landmark that welcomes visitors to explore its history.
cards.source_title: Old Capitol Museum | The University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Check the museum's current hours and visit information before going.

cards.title: Try a recreation activity at the CRWC
cards.subtitle: 309 S. Madison Street
cards.notes: Check current facility access and activity times, then choose from fitness, courts, track, climbing, or aquatic spaces that fit your plan.
cards.short_summary: A large Student Life recreation facility with fitness, climbing, court, track, and pool spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UI Recreational Services lists fitness space, a climbing wall, pools, a jogging track, basketball and volleyball courts, and a multi-activity gym at the CRWC.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation and Wellness Center | University of Iowa Recreational Services
cards.access_notes: Review current CRWC hours and applicable membership or guest-access requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Visit a community-centered study and gathering space
cards.subtitle: Pride Alliance Center, 601 Melrose Ave.
cards.notes: Check the posted weekday hours, then use the living room, study rooms, games, or computer and printer in this student and community venue.
cards.short_summary: The Pride Alliance Center's house includes social, study, and practical resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UI says Pride House serves students, student organizations, and community members, with study rooms, a living room, computer and printer, games, and a kitchen.
cards.source_title: Facilities | University of Iowa Leadership and Engagement
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday–Thursday 3–9 p.m. and Friday 12–5 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Use the low-sensory lounge when you need calm
cards.subtitle: University Capitol Centre
cards.notes: Stop by for a lower-sensory place to reset or work, and consult Student Disability Services if you need support or accommodation guidance.
cards.short_summary: An all-student low-sensory study and reset space managed by Student Disability Services.
cards.evidence_claim: University Classrooms identifies the SDS Lounge in University Capitol Centre as a low-sensory space dedicated to students with disabilities and open to all students.
cards.source_title: Student Learning Spaces | University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; confirm building access and any current lounge guidance before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission, under-21-safe ways to spend time on campus and in Iowa City.

cards.title: Walk the Stanley galleries
cards.subtitle: 160 W. Burlington St. · Iowa City
cards.notes: Meet in the lobby, choose a floor, and take a self-paced lap through the galleries. Check the museum’s visit page for current opening days.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop with changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Stanley Museum of Art is always free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Stanley Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open hours and scheduled closures are listed on the museum visit page; admission ends five minutes before gallery closing.

cards.entity_name: Stanley Museum of Art Touch Tour
cards.title: Book a Stanley touch tour
cards.subtitle: Stanley Museum of Art · Iowa City
cards.notes: For visitors who are blind or partially sighted and companions, arrange an educator-led tactile gallery visit in advance for a focused group outing.
cards.short_summary: An appointment-based tactile museum experience.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stanley offers free touch tours by appointment for visitors who are blind or partially sighted and their companions.
cards.source_title: Accessibility | Stanley Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Available by appointment in groups of three plus companions; the museum requests four weeks’ advance notice.

cards.title: Explore Old Capitol Museum
cards.subtitle: 21 N. Clinton St. · Iowa City
cards.notes: Use a self-guided visit to move through the historic building and exhibits together. Groups of more than 10 are asked to schedule ahead.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided museum visit on the Pentacrest.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Capitol Museum self-guided visits have no charge and museum admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | Old Capitol Museum
cards.access_notes: Self-guided visits are self-paced; the museum asks groups larger than 10 to schedule in advance.

cards.title: Browse Iowa Hall
cards.subtitle: Museum of Natural History · Macbride Hall
cards.notes: Set a meet-up point at Macbride Hall, then explore Iowa Hall at your own pace. Larger self-guided groups should reserve ahead.
cards.short_summary: A named gallery within the free Museum of Natural History.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa Hall is available for no-charge self-guided visits, and Museum of Natural History admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Iowa Hall for self-guided visits and asks groups of more than 10 to schedule in advance.

cards.title: Look through Bird Hall
cards.subtitle: Museum of Natural History · Macbride Hall
cards.notes: Plan a slow loop through Bird Hall and compare what each person notices. Keep the visit self-guided to retain the no-charge access.
cards.short_summary: A named natural-history gallery for a self-paced visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Bird Hall is available for no-charge self-guided visits, and Museum of Natural History admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Bird Hall for self-guided visits and asks groups of more than 10 to schedule in advance.

cards.title: Tour Mammal Hall at your pace
cards.subtitle: Museum of Natural History · Macbride Hall
cards.notes: Make Mammal Hall the destination for a short between-classes stop or a longer museum wander. No ticket purchase is needed for self-guided entry.
cards.short_summary: A free named gallery in Macbride Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Mammal Hall is available for no-charge self-guided visits, and Museum of Natural History admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Mammal Hall for self-guided visits and asks groups of more than 10 to schedule in advance.

cards.title: Check out a TREKsack
cards.subtitle: Iowa Hall front desk · Macbride Hall
cards.notes: Ask at the Iowa Hall front desk for a free TREKsack, then use its books and sensory tools while exploring the Museum of Natural History.
cards.short_summary: A free interactive museum-kit checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: TREKsacks are free to check out at the Iowa Hall front desk.
cards.source_title: TREKsacks | University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Ask the Iowa Hall front desk about availability; the program includes sensory-support items and books.

cards.title: See the Main Library Gallery
cards.subtitle: Main Library north entrance · Iowa City
cards.notes: Enter through the Main Library’s north entrance and take in the current exhibition together. Pair it with a free gallery talk when one is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A public exhibition space for rare objects and archives.
cards.evidence_claim: All Main Library Gallery exhibits and associated programming are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit to the Main Library Gallery
cards.access_notes: General-public visitors may stop by during open hours; access is via the Main Library’s north entrance.

cards.title: Take a greenhouse reset
cards.subtitle: Biology Building East, fourth floor
cards.notes: Visit the fourth-floor greenhouse with a friend for a quiet plant-filled break. Call ahead if you want to arrange a group tour.
cards.short_summary: A public indoor plant collection above downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biology Greenhouse is open to the general public on weekdays, and the university identifies it among campus experiences with free admission.
cards.source_title: Three Things You Need to Experience on the University of Iowa Campus
cards.access_notes: Open to the general public weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m; closed on university holidays. Call ahead for group tours.

cards.title: Ride an Iowa City Transit route
cards.subtitle: Iowa City Transit · Iowa City
cards.notes: Choose a route, ride to a nearby stop, and make the trip itself the hang. Confirm route-specific service times before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A fare-free way to move around Iowa City.
cards.evidence_claim: Bus fares are free in Iowa City through the Fare Free Iowa City pilot.
cards.source_title: Fares and Passes | Iowa City
cards.access_notes: Iowa City Transit operates 13 fixed routes Monday through Saturday; service hours vary by route.

warnings: Museum and transit schedules can change; check the linked official pages before heading out.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented University of Iowa study environments, from reservable collaboration rooms to quiet library seating.

cards.title: Main Library Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Main Library, first floor
cards.notes: Set up at a movable table or lounge seat, then use the nearby Just Ask Desk for a weekday drop-in research consultation.
cards.short_summary: Flexible first-floor seating with academic help and technology resources nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: The first-floor Learning Commons has lounge seating, movable tables, electrical outlets, reservable rooms, and a research-help desk.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons — University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Main Library; consult the library’s current open-hours listing before visiting.

cards.title: Learning Commons Group Spaces
cards.subtitle: Main Library, first-floor Learning Commons
cards.notes: Reserve online for a project session with at least one other student; plan for a two-hour maximum and claim the room on time.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms for collaborative work in the Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Learning Commons group spaces are reservable by students, require groups of two or more, and allow reservations of up to two hours.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons group spaces — University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Student reservations use Office 365, HealthcareOWA, or room touchscreens; unclaimed reservations are forfeited after 10 minutes.

cards.entity_name: Main Library Undergraduate Short-Term Study Rooms
cards.title: Undergraduate Short-Term Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Main Library
cards.notes: Bring your Iowa One Card to the first-floor Service Desk and request a key when you need a solo, short-term workspace.
cards.short_summary: Individual rooms for current undergraduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Current UI undergraduates may use individual Main Library rooms on a first-come, first-served basis for four-hour short-term study.
cards.source_title: Main Library study spaces and locker information — University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available when Main Library collections are open; one undergraduate per room, with a key collected and returned at the Service Desk.

cards.entity_name: Third-Floor Current and Bound Journals Quiet Seating
cards.title: Third-Floor Journal Seating
cards.subtitle: Main Library, east side of third floor
cards.notes: Choose a seat around the current and bound journals for individual work, and keep conversation to a whisper if needed.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet zone among the Main Library’s journal collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The east side of the Main Library’s third floor around current and bound journals is designated quiet study seating.
cards.source_title: Main Library study spaces and locker information — University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: This is a quiet-study area: whispered conversations and individual work are permitted.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Bookstacks Seating
cards.subtitle: Main Library, east and west bookstacks
cards.notes: Head to either bookstack side on the fourth floor when you want individual work in a designated quiet-study area.
cards.short_summary: Quiet seating tucked into the Main Library’s fourth-floor stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Both the east and west bookstack areas on the Main Library’s fourth floor are designated quiet study seating.
cards.source_title: Main Library study spaces and locker information — University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Quiet-study expectations apply: individual work is permitted and conversations should be whispered.

cards.title: Fifth-Floor Bookstacks Seating
cards.subtitle: Main Library, east and west bookstacks
cards.notes: Use a fifth-floor stack-side seat for a quiet individual session, keeping calls and regular conversation in the central corridors.
cards.short_summary: A second quiet bookstack setting on the Main Library’s upper floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Both the east and west bookstack areas on the Main Library’s fifth floor are designated quiet study seating.
cards.source_title: Main Library study spaces and locker information — University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Quiet-study expectations apply; the library directs phone calls and conversations to central corridors.

cards.entity_name: Lichtenberger Engineering Library Pod 1 and Pod 2
cards.title: Engineering Library Study Pods
cards.subtitle: Lichtenberger Engineering Library
cards.notes: Reserve a pod with your HawkID for a small-group session; use the Solstice display to share a laptop, tablet, or phone screen.
cards.short_summary: Two small reservable rooms built for screen-sharing collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Pod 1 and Pod 2 each seat four to five people and include Solstice wireless-collaboration technology.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms — Lichtenberger Engineering Library
cards.access_notes: Reserve through Office 365 using a HawkID; the library’s group-space rules and current hours apply.

cards.title: Engineering Library Creative Space
cards.subtitle: Lichtenberger Engineering Library
cards.notes: Bring a larger project group to the movable tables and whiteboards, and check whether a workshop has the space in use first.
cards.short_summary: A flexible project room with large monitors, whiteboards, and maker equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Engineering Library Creative Space has large monitors, whiteboards, movable tables, and is first-come, first-served for students when not closed for workshops.
cards.source_title: Find a study space — Lichtenberger Engineering Library
cards.access_notes: Open to students on a first-come, first-served basis; it may be unavailable during workshops.

cards.entity_name: Lichtenberger Engineering Library Lower-Level Silent Study
cards.title: Engineering Library Lower-Level Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Lichtenberger Engineering Library, lower level
cards.notes: Take a carrel, armchair, beanbag, or gaming chair downstairs when you need a silent setting with power for your equipment.
cards.short_summary: Silent lower-level seating with carrels and varied chair options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Engineering Library’s downstairs level is silent study space with carrels, armchairs, beanbag chairs, and gaming chairs.
cards.source_title: Find a study space — Lichtenberger Engineering Library
cards.access_notes: The source distinguishes this silent lower level from the main floor, where talking is allowed.

cards.title: Hubbard Commons
cards.subtitle: Iowa Memorial Union
cards.notes: Settle near the fireplace for an individual study block, then use IMU WiFi or move to an ITC if you need a campus computer.
cards.short_summary: Fireplace-adjacent IMU seating with WiFi and nearby computing options.
cards.evidence_claim: The Iowa Memorial Union identifies Hubbard Commons as a fireplace-side study setting and offers WiFi, ITCs, and additional tables and couches.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces — Iowa Memorial Union
cards.access_notes: The IMU states that a HawkID is required for ITCs and wireless internet; check current building hours before visiting.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named downtown Iowa City stops immediately beside the University of Iowa campus, each tied to its stated corridor.

cards.title: Prairie Lights Books: catch an in-store reading
cards.subtitle: South Dubuque Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the store’s current event listing before you go, then browse the shelves at 15 S. Dubuque Street.
cards.short_summary: A downtown bookstore with scheduled in-store author and community readings.
cards.evidence_claim: Prairie Lights Books lists its Iowa City address at 15 S. Dubuque St. and publishes upcoming in-store events.
cards.source_title: Prairie Lights Books — Home Page
cards.access_notes: Store hours and event details are posted by Prairie Lights; confirm the specific event before visiting.

cards.title: Iowa City Public Library: use the downtown library
cards.subtitle: South Linn Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 123 S. Linn Street for a library visit; check the library calendar for the day’s public programs.
cards.short_summary: A public library with downtown hours, digital resources, and a frequently updated events calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: The Iowa City Public Library is at 123 South Linn Street and lists public hours from Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Iowa City Public Library — Hours & Location
cards.access_notes: Current listed hours are Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–9 p.m., Friday 10 a.m.–8 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; verify holiday changes.

cards.title: FilmScene on the Ped Mall: see a programmed film
cards.subtitle: East College Street / Pedestrian Mall corridor
cards.notes: Choose a current screening and reserve a seat online or at the box office at 118 E. College Street.
cards.short_summary: A two-screen nonprofit cinema in a restored downtown building on the Ped Mall.
cards.evidence_claim: FilmScene identifies its Ped Mall cinema at 118 E. College St. and describes its two-screen restored historic venue.
cards.source_title: FilmScene — The Ped Mall
cards.access_notes: The box office opens one hour before the first showtime; consult FilmScene’s current calendar for screenings and ticket details.

cards.title: Riverside Theatre: plan for live theatre
cards.subtitle: East College Street corridor
cards.notes: Review the current production schedule, then use the theatre’s visit page for box-office and accessibility details.
cards.short_summary: A professional theatre company with its box office and performance venue on East College Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Riverside Theatre lists its Iowa City venue and box office at 119 E. College Street.
cards.source_title: Riverside Theatre — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Box-office hours listed are Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; performance access and ticket requirements vary by production.

cards.title: The Englert Theatre: check the marquee schedule
cards.subtitle: East Washington Street corridor
cards.notes: Look over the current event calendar, then use the street-level entrance beneath the marquee at 221 E. Washington.
cards.short_summary: A downtown theatre venue with a street-level marquee and box office.
cards.evidence_claim: The Englert Theatre states that it is located at 221 E. Washington Street in downtown Iowa City.
cards.source_title: The Englert Theatre — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: The box office lists Tuesday hours of 10 a.m.–6 p.m., Wednesday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m., and opening one hour before most performances.

cards.title: Iowa Artisans Gallery: view handcrafted work
cards.subtitle: East Washington Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse the gallery’s current handcrafted work at 207 E. Washington Street and check its site for pop-up-hour changes.
cards.short_summary: A gallery and shop presenting handcrafted work by artists from Iowa and beyond.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa Artisans Gallery lists its address at 207 E. Washington St. and says it celebrates artists’ creativity and craftsmanship.
cards.source_title: Iowa Artisans Gallery
cards.access_notes: Listed regular hours are Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–5:30 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; the gallery advises checking for pop-up hours.

cards.title: Record Collector: browse physical music
cards.subtitle: South Linn Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse new and used vinyl at 116 S. Linn Street; use the store’s online inventory if you are seeking a particular item.
cards.short_summary: A downtown record shop selling new and used vinyl, CDs, and special orders.
cards.evidence_claim: Record Collector says it has operated at 116 South Linn Street since 2007 and specializes in new and used vinyl.
cards.source_title: Record Collector — History
cards.access_notes: The business posts its standard hours online and notes that holiday or weather changes are announced on its door, social channels, and Google listing.

cards.title: Public Space One NorthSIDE: visit a gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: North Gilbert Street corridor
cards.notes: Check PS1’s event information and gallery hours, then visit the exhibition space at 229 N. Gilbert Street.
cards.short_summary: A downtown nonprofit arts space with gallery exhibitions, a press co-op, and artist studios.
cards.evidence_claim: Public Space One identifies its NorthSIDE gallery at 229 N. Gilbert and lists gallery exhibitions among its uses.
cards.source_title: Public Space One — Location + Contact
cards.access_notes: The listed gallery hours are Friday 4–6 p.m. and Saturday noon–3 p.m.; PS1 asks visitors to check its homepage for event and access updates.

cards.title: Iowa City Farmers Market: follow the seasonal stalls
cards.subtitle: East Washington Street / Chauncey Swan corridor
cards.notes: Visit the 400 block of East Washington on a Saturday in season and use the city’s vendor map to locate stalls.
cards.short_summary: A city-managed open-air market spanning the Chauncey Swan ramp, park, and East Washington Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Iowa City places the market at 415 E. Washington St. and schedules its 2026 season on Saturdays from May 2 through October 31.
cards.source_title: City of Iowa City — Iowa City Farmers Market
cards.access_notes: For the 2026 season, the city lists Saturday hours of 7:30 a.m.–noon, May 2–October 31; individual vendors and purchases vary.

cards.title: City Plaza: walk the Pedestrian Mall
cards.subtitle: Pedestrian Mall / South Dubuque Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the walk-only plaza as a downtown connector, and check the district calendar for public art, shops, and scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian-only downtown plaza with shops, dining, public art, and year-round events.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Iowa Student Life describes the Pedestrian Mall as a walk-only downtown district with shops, dining, public art, and year-round events.
cards.source_title: University of Iowa Student Life — Fall highlights in and around Iowa City
cards.access_notes: The plaza is an outdoor pedestrian district; event programming and individual business access vary, so consult current listings before a specific visit.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Iowa traditions, from the Kinnick Stadium wave to Homecoming’s corn monument and campus songs.

cards.title: Turn toward the children’s hospital
cards.subtitle: Kinnick Stadium, end of the first quarter
cards.notes: At the end of the first quarter of a home football game, turn toward the children’s hospital and join the crowd in waving.
cards.short_summary: A stadium-wide greeting for pediatric patients and families watching from the hospital.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa Athletics says the Hawkeye Wave began in 2017 and has fans turn toward UI Stead Family Children’s Hospital when the first-quarter clock reaches zero.
cards.source_title: The Hawkeye Wave | Iowa Hawkeyes Athletics
cards.access_notes: Occurs during University of Iowa home football games at Kinnick Stadium.

cards.entity_name: University of Iowa Homecoming Corn Monument
cards.title: Find the Pentacrest built in corn
cards.subtitle: Pentacrest during Homecoming Week
cards.notes: Walk the Pentacrest during Homecoming Week to see that year’s large-scale structure, assembled from corn by student teams.
cards.short_summary: A changing Homecoming installation that turns Iowa corn into a campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Iowa Honors Program describes the annual Homecoming corn monument on the Pentacrest as a tradition involving engineering and other students.
cards.source_title: ‘It’s Corn!’: A Look Into the 2024 Hawkeye Homecoming Monument
cards.access_notes: The monument is a Homecoming Week feature; consult the current Homecoming schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Watch the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Downtown Iowa City during Homecoming Week
cards.notes: Use the current Homecoming schedule to pick a parade-viewing spot downtown and watch alumni, bands, floats, and campus groups pass.
cards.short_summary: The public procession anchoring Iowa’s annual Homecoming celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Iowa Homecoming site identifies the parade as part of its annual Homecoming events and says it draws more than 20,000 spectators.
cards.source_title: University of Iowa Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Check the official Homecoming site for the current route, date, and start time.

cards.title: Gather for the coronation
cards.subtitle: University of Iowa Homecoming Thursday night
cards.notes: Attend the Thursday Homecoming gathering to hear scholarship recipients announced and see the Homecoming Royalty crowned.
cards.short_summary: A Thursday-night Homecoming ceremony combining a pep rally with recognition and coronation.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Iowa Homecoming describes the Pep Rally and Coronation as a Thursday-night celebration that announces scholarship recipients and crowns Homecoming Royalty.
cards.source_title: University of Iowa Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Refer to the official Homecoming schedule for the current venue and participation details.

cards.title: Look through a century of buttons
cards.subtitle: Homecoming button archive
cards.notes: Browse the virtual button archive and compare designs from different years; the physical collection is held at the Iowa Memorial Union.
cards.short_summary: Annual Homecoming buttons preserved as Hawkeye collectibles and historical artifacts.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Iowa Homecoming says buttons have traditionally been made each year and its archive spans designs from 1924 to the present.
cards.source_title: History | University of Iowa Homecoming
cards.access_notes: The official history page links to the virtual archive; button availability varies by year.

cards.title: Learn “Old Gold”
cards.subtitle: University of Iowa school-song tradition
cards.notes: Listen for “Old Gold” in Iowa’s school-song history, then use the Music Library’s account to trace its early campus role.
cards.short_summary: A 1905 school song adopted through a University of Iowa contest.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Iowa Rita Benton Music Library identifies “Old Gold” as a 1905 school song that assumed a role in campus life and Hawkeye Marching Band traditions.
cards.source_title: A brief history of school songs at the University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Read the Music Library history for background and documented lyrics context.

cards.title: Trace “On Iowa”
cards.subtitle: University of Iowa school-song tradition
cards.notes: Use the Music Library’s school-song history to place “On Iowa” in the sequence of songs adopted into Hawkeye campus life.
cards.short_summary: A 1917 Iowa song with an established role in campus and marching-band traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Iowa Rita Benton Music Library lists “On Iowa” (1917) among songs that assumed distinct roles in campus life and Hawkeye Marching Band traditions.
cards.source_title: A brief history of school songs at the University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Read the Music Library history for the song’s documented campus context.

cards.title: Recognize “The Iowa Fight Song”
cards.subtitle: University of Iowa school-song tradition
cards.notes: Follow the Music Library’s historical overview to identify “The Iowa Fight Song” and its place among Iowa’s longstanding songs.
cards.short_summary: A 1950 school song embedded in Iowa campus and Hawkeye Marching Band tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Iowa Rita Benton Music Library identifies “The Iowa Fight Song” (1950) as one of the songs with distinct roles in campus life and Hawkeye Marching Band traditions.
cards.source_title: A brief history of school songs at the University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Read the Music Library history for the song’s documented campus context.

cards.title: Follow “Roll Along, Iowa”
cards.subtitle: University of Iowa school-song tradition
cards.notes: Explore the Music Library’s school-song history to see how “Roll Along, Iowa” fits the Hawkeye Marching Band’s repertoire.
cards.short_summary: A 1954 University of Iowa song with a documented role in campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Iowa Rita Benton Music Library lists “Roll Along, Iowa” (1954) among songs that assumed distinct roles in campus life and Hawkeye Marching Band traditions.
cards.source_title: A brief history of school songs at the University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Read the Music Library history for the song’s documented campus context.

cards.title: Meet Iowa’s alma mater
cards.subtitle: Also known as The Hawkeye Hymn
cards.notes: Read the University Archives guide for the alma mater’s credited lyricist, composition date, and alternate Hawkeye song names.
cards.short_summary: The University of Iowa alma mater, also called “The Hawkeye Hymn” and “The Iowa Alumni Song.”
cards.evidence_claim: University of Iowa Libraries identifies “Alma Mater, Iowa” as also known as “The Hawkeye Hymn” and “The Iowa Alumni Song,” with lyrics by Gene Mills and a 1960 composition.
cards.source_title: University Archives: Resource Guide to University Traditions and Songs
cards.access_notes: The University Archives guide provides the documented song history and lyrics reference.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Iowa, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that starts with campus landmarks, builds in museums and study space, and finishes with low-key Iowa City exploration.

cards.title: Start with the Pentacrest
cards.subtitle: Campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Walk the lawn boundary from Clinton to Madison and Washington to Jefferson, then use Old Capitol at its center to get your bearings.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the campus landscape that frames Old Capitol and academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The university identifies the Pentacrest as the area bounded by Clinton, Washington, Madison, and Jefferson streets, with Old Capitol at its center.
cards.source_title: The Pentacrest | Iowa Memorial Union
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; events and classes may be scheduled there.

cards.title: Step inside Old Capitol
cards.subtitle: 21 N. Clinton St.
cards.notes: Continue from the lawn into the museum and take a self-guided look at the galleries and history panels during public open hours.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus-building visit with a self-guided option.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Capitol Museum is open to the public with always-free admission, and visitors may take self-guided tours during open hours.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | Old Capitol Museum
cards.access_notes: Self-guided visits are available during open hours; groups of more than 10 should schedule ahead.

cards.entity_name: University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.title: Browse Macbride Hall galleries
cards.subtitle: 11 Macbride Hall
cards.notes: Make this your next indoor stop and explore the Iowa, Bird, and Mammal halls at your own pace while the museum is open.
cards.short_summary: Natural-history galleries a short walk from Old Capitol.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Natural History is open to the public with always-free admission; its self-guided galleries include Iowa, Bird, and Mammal halls.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Wednesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm holiday exceptions before going.

cards.title: Pick a Main Library study spot
cards.subtitle: 125 W. Washington St.
cards.notes: Pause for a plan-your-week session: choose a quiet seat or meet up in a group-study area, then check the library’s current access details.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus reset with quiet, group, and technology-enabled spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: University sources list quiet and group study spaces, computers, and an active learning area in the Main Library.
cards.source_title: Student Learning Spaces | University Classrooms
cards.access_notes: Listed public building hours include until 1 a.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday; hours exclude holidays, breaks, and special events.

cards.title: See what is on at the Stanley
cards.subtitle: 160 W. Burlington St.
cards.notes: Walk south from the library, check the gallery plan, and give yourself time to look closely rather than trying to see every room.
cards.short_summary: A free art-museum stop beside the Main Library and Gibson Square Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stanley Museum of Art is adjacent to Gibson Square Park and the Main Library, and admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Stanley Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours vary by day; the museum states that admission ends five minutes before gallery closing.

cards.title: Use the IMU as your campus hub
cards.subtitle: 125 N. Madison St.
cards.notes: Stop at the Welcome Center or settle into a public study area, and check renovation updates before depending on a particular room or service.
cards.short_summary: A central student-life building with study spaces, services, and changing renovation conditions.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes the IMU as centrally located and lists study spaces, Wi-Fi, computer labs, dining options, and the Learning Commons.
cards.source_title: Student Learning Spaces | University Classrooms
cards.access_notes: The IMU reports renovations in progress; verify building hours and the availability of specific spaces before arrival.

cards.title: Move at the CRWC
cards.subtitle: 309 S. Madison St.
cards.notes: If you have facility access, choose a low-pressure activity such as the track, pool, or open recreation; review entry and facility hours first.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with fitness, pool, track, and court facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The CRWC includes fitness space, a climbing wall, pools, a jogging track, and basketball/volleyball courts.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation and Wellness Center | Recreational Services
cards.access_notes: Recreational Services lists paid daily walk-ins and membership access; check current hours and eligibility before visiting.

cards.title: Walk out to Hancher Green
cards.subtitle: Outside Hancher Auditorium, 141 Park Rd.
cards.notes: Use the riverside lawn as a breather between stops, then check Hancher’s current calendar for any all-ages outdoor program you may want to attend.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor performance-lawn destination beside Hancher Auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Hancher identifies Hancher Green as the outdoor location at Hancher Auditorium, 141 Park Road, and has hosted all-ages public events there.
cards.source_title: Hancher Green event information | Hancher Auditorium
cards.access_notes: Outdoor events and ticketing vary; consult Hancher’s current event listing before making plans.

cards.title: Cross downtown to the public library
cards.subtitle: 123 S. Linn St., downtown Iowa City
cards.notes: Settle in with a book, browse a floor, or use this as a calm meet-up point before your group heads back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: A downtown reading-and-regrouping stop with published daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa City Public Library lists its downtown location at 123 South Linn Street and publishes hours every day of the week.
cards.source_title: Hours & Location | Iowa City Public Library
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–9 p.m., Friday 10 a.m.–8 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; special closures apply.

cards.title: End on the Literary Walk
cards.subtitle: Downtown Iowa City sidewalks
cards.notes: Finish by following the city’s Literary Walk map and pausing at bronze sidewalk panels; it is an easy way to notice the downtown on foot.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced public-art walk that connects downtown streets with Iowa City’s writing culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Iowa City lists an Iowa City Literary Walk Map within its public-art resources and describes bronze panels installed along Iowa Avenue.
cards.source_title: Your Public Art | City of Iowa City
cards.access_notes: Use the city’s Literary Walk map and stay on public sidewalks; allow extra time if stopping to read panels.
